details: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) introduced "Regulation Crypto Assets" on August 18, 2026. This new framework proposes two exemptions for crypto asset offerings—allowing fundraising up to $5 million over four years or $75 million annually—along with a conditional safe harbor. The initiative aims to create clear pathways for capital formation and foster innovation within the U.S. crypto markets while maintaining investor protections.
title: SEC Proposes "Regulation Crypto Assets" Framework

details: On August 18, 2026, Bitcoin saw a notable rally, jumping approximately 2.5% to around $64,400. This surge followed the release of weaker-than-expected U.S. July retail sales, which fell by 0.6% month-on-month. The unexpected slowdown in consumer spending eased fears of more aggressive monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, prompting a rotation of macro funds into risk assets, including Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies.
title: Bitcoin Rallies as Weak US Retail Sales Data Cools Fed Hike Expectations

details: A 2026 study, citing data from the Atlantic Council's CBDC Tracker, indicates that over 130 countries, accounting for 98% of global GDP, are actively exploring or piloting Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs). Nations like China are at the forefront, leveraging CBDCs to modernize financial systems and potentially reduce reliance on the U.S. dollar. The Eurozone is expected to make a decision on a digital euro by late 2026, while the U.S. has legislated against the Federal Reserve issuing a retail CBDC via the GENIUS Act.
title: Over 130 Countries Exploring CBDCs in 2026, Atlantic Council Reports

details: Financial markets are showing caution ahead of the Federal Reserve's July meeting minutes, set to be released on August 19, 2026. This anticipation comes amidst a challenging macro environment, with the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield reaching its highest level in 19 years and crude oil prices climbing above $90 per barrel, reigniting inflation concerns. Bitcoin and broader cryptocurrency markets are trading range-bound, highly sensitive to any indications from the Fed regarding its future stance on inflation, economic growth, and financial conditions.
title: FOMC Minutes Awaited as Elevated Yields & Oil Prices Drive Market Caution
